subject: Request: region-binding exemption for legacy ERP integration + rollout gates
messages:
From: Tom Blake <tom.blake@acme-erp.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: sanjay.rao@acme-erp.com, procurement@acme-erp.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: region-binding exemption for legacy ERP integration

Hi Stephanie,

Quick note from the Acme integration team: our on-prem legacy ERP connector can only talk to a single pinned model instance in the us-west region due to strict network egress rules and an embedded inference client that does not support automatic fallback. The alternative is a rewrite that will take months.

Because of that constraint we need a short-term exception to Redwood's routing/fallback policy so calls from our connector are forced to a dedicated endpoint (no automatic fallback to other variants or regions). We understand this increases operational risk; we're willing to sign an SLA addendum and follow a rollback/runbook you require.

Questions we have:
- Can Redwood provide a pinned endpoint (us-west) with no-fallback for ACME-ERP for an initial 8-week pilot?
- What's the process for exception approval, and what operational controls do you need from us?

Attached is a simplified network diagram and a proposed escalation matrix.

Thanks,
Tom Blake
Head of Integrations, Acme ERP
attachments: acme-connection-diagram.pdf, escalation_matrix.xlsx

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Tom Blake <tom.blake@acme-erp.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: region-binding exemption for legacy ERP integration

Tom — thanks for the clear context and the attachments. I'm looping in Product (Lauren), Ops (Marcus), and Routing policy (Karthik) to scope the request and the gating we would need. High level: we can consider a temporary "no-fallback" endpoint but need to align on ownerable runbook, rollout gates, and a rollback timeline.

Immediate asks from my side:
- Lauren: product clarity on long-term compatibility and any quality/regression concerns if we force a single variant.
- Marcus: capacity and monitoring implications for a pinned dedicated endpoint (SLOs, cost).
- Karthik: any policy risks and approval path for a region-binding exemption.

I'll coordinate a quick sync for Monday.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Manager, Solutions — Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, Tom Blake <tom.blake@acme-erp.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: region-binding exemption for legacy ERP integration

Thanks for the details, Tom and Stephanie. Product perspective: forcing a single model/region is workable short-term but we have a few caveats:

1) Model selection: we need to pin to a compatible variant that is both compliant with Acme's data profile and supported by our runtime (I recommend the rwd-instruct-3b-q4 variant for latency/cost parity).
2) Quality & evals: we will need a small regression test set that Acme signs off on — we can't silently ship a variant that degrades outputs for critical ticketing flows.
3) Rollout gates: we require a staged rollout (staging -> canary -> full) with explicit sign-off at each gate and an automatic automatic rollback on defined error thresholds.

Operational ask: if the connector truly cannot handle fallbacks, Ops must own a hot standby plan and we will require a documented rollback window (we recommend 48 hours).

If Acme can accept those constraints, Product can support a timeboxed exemption (8–12 weeks) while they work on an SDK update. We'll also require a written addendum that specifies data residency, retention, and indemnity clauses.

— Lauren Bishop
VP, Product — Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: region-binding exemption for legacy ERP integration

Operational notes and proposed plan:

- Capacity: we can carve a small dedicated pool in us-west. Estimated baseline is 2x V100-equivalents for the pilot (based on their traffic profile). Cost/time to provision: 48 hours from approval.
- Monitoring: we'll add per-endpoint traces, token-level cost alerts, and a synthetic check that verifies inputs/outputs every 5 minutes. We'll require access to Acme's test harness for the canary stage.
- Runbook & rollback: SRE will own a documented rollback that does an immediate route remove and failover to a maintenance page; we will target a 30-minute recovery window once rollback is initiated.
- Security/compliance: need to confirm whether Acme wants a Private deployment (VPC) or a Dedicated tenancy; if Private, timeline shifts.

Next steps I propose:
1) Stephanie to confirm which model variant Acme agrees to (Product to provide variant list).
2) Acme to sign the operational addendum and provide test harness access.
3) Ops to provision and run gated canary.

I'll create the runbook draft after we get confirmation.

— Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

From: Tom Blake <tom.blake@acme-erp.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, procurement@acme-erp.com, sanjay.rao@acme-erp.com
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: region-binding exemption for legacy ERP integration

Folks — appreciate the quick triage and the clear list of asks. Acme approves the rwd-instruct-3b-q4 variant recommendation and we can provide the test harness and a signed addendum. Procurement copied here — please keep me posted on the DocuSign link.

Couple of commitments from our side:
- We'll provide the staging test harness by Friday EOD and a point-of-contact for SRE (Sanjay Rao).
- We'll accept the 48-hour rollback window and the 30-minute recovery SLA as part of the operational plan for the pilot.

Please send the DocuSign and the runbook draft when ready so we can review and sign off.

Regards,
Tom
Head of Integrations, Acme ERP
attachments: none
